reasons: The code measures the haploid (gametophytic) chromosome number n per species (from the CCDB 'median' column) and computes the shares with n<6, 6<=n<=16, and n>16, which matches the claim’s quantities and thresholds. The data modality (a large compilation of species-level chromosome counts) is appropriate for a claim about the distribution of chromosome numbers. Assumptions introduce some risk: a single global decision about whether the 'median' column is at n or 2n based on six references could mis-scale species if the API mixes levels across taxa, and using the median per species can be influenced by polyploid cytotypes rather than a canonical count. The pre-registered criteria (>=70% in-range, upper tail < lower tail, and upper tail <15%) directly operationalize “mostly… few… fewer still” and would distinguish the claim from plausible alternatives. The narrowing to plants is explicit in the hypothesis and data description, so the result pertains to plants rather than all organisms as in the original statement.
what_would_change_it: Include comparable animal chromosome-number data to test the cross-kingdom claim, and harmonize all records to haploid n using per-record n/2n indicators rather than a single global switch. Pre-register a canonical-species-value rule (e.g., lowest reported haploid count or curated consensus) to handle multiple cytotypes within species.
